shared_elements: frontal standing/upright human-like figure filling the whole surface
large elaborate headdress occupying the upper part of the monument
carved relief on a tall upright slab-shaped stone
curvilinear scroll motifs around the head and torso
chest/pectoral ornament with a disc or oval element
arms held across the front of the body
band or belt across the lower torso
justification: Both depict a single frontal upright figure occupying an entire tall slab, with a heavy headdress above, scrollwork flanking the head, arms folded across the chest, a disc-like pectoral and a belt band low on the torso — a specific and shared vertical scheme. The biggest difference is density and legibility of detail: A is crowded with small subsidiary faces, dangling ornaments and interlocking motifs and shows a clear naturalistic human face with legs and feet, whereas B is highly reduced, faceless in the visible view, with sparse shallow scrolls and no lower limbs shown.
